text.p: Tropical Cyclone Ophelia, with 50 mph winds, is south of Java in the Southeast Indian Ocean near 10.5s/109.0e, moving east at 3 mph. A turn to the southeast is expected as Ophelia rapidly intensifies. Top winds should reach 100 mph by 48 hours as the system becomes a major threat to shipping. It is a few days away from the coast of Northwest Australia, should it take the track it is expected to take.

Tropical Depression 41W is in the far Southern South China sea near 4n/110e, moving east at 8 mph. Top winds are near 30 mph and should change little during the next 24-36 hours as the storm becomes nearly stationary then begins to drift westward. This system will be a moderate threat to shipping but it no threat to major land areas at this time.
THERE ARE NO FURTHER EMERGENCY WEATHER STATEMENTS
